summary: Henry Harkness (1790–1838) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as secretary at the College of Fort St. George until 1834, and later as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from 1834 to 1837.

Henry Hart Milman (1791–1868) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at Eton and Brasenose College, Oxford, under adviser Horace Hayman Wilson, he served as Professor of Poetry at the University of Oxford from 1821 to 1831.

Henry Heras (1888–1955) worked in Indology and history/archaeology after studying at Col·legi del Sagrat Cor. He taught at Colegio del Salvador (1921–1922) and became a professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, in 1923, founding the Heras Institute in 1926.

Henry Herbert Dodwell (1879–1946) was a scholar of Indology and history. Educated at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford, he served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and as professor at SOAS University of London (1922–1946).

Henry Hoenigswald (1915–2003) was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence under Giacomo Devoto. He taught at Yale, Hartford Seminary, and served as Associate Professor of Linguistics at the University of Pennsylvania (1948–1985).

Henry Hughes Presler (1908–1998) worked in religious studies and Indology. Educated at North Dakota State, Boston, and Chicago universities, he was a missionary for the United Methodist Board (1937–1972) and held a post at Leonard Theological College (~1947–1972).

Henry James Sumner Maine (1822–1888) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology educated at Pembroke College, Cambridge. He was Regius Professor of Civil Law at Cambridge (1847–1854) and Corpus Professor of Jurisprudence at Oxford (1871–1878).

Henry Lee Shuttleworth (1882–1960) worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Pembroke College, Oxford, and the University of Cambridge, and later served as Lecturer in Tibetan at SOAS University of London (1936–1948).
Henry Martyn (1781–1812) was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Truro Cathedral School, St John's College (~1797–1801), and under John Borthwick Gilchrist (~1804–1805).
Henry Miers Elliot (1808–1853) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Winchester College. He served as a civil servant for the East India Company from circa 1826 until 1853.

Henry Morris (1829–1912) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Rugby School and the East India Company College before serving in the Madras Civil Service as Judge of Godavery from 1848 to 1875.

Henry Nelson Wright (1869–1941) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied classics at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1888–1892), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1892–1925), and founded the Numismatic Society of India in 1910.

Henry Octavius Coxe (1811–1881) was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at Westminster School and Worcester College before working at the British Museum (1833–1838) and serving as Librarian at the Bodleian Library from 1839 to 1881.

Henry Pitts Forster (1766–1815) worked in Indology and linguistics. He joined the Bengal Civil Service and East India Company in 1783, later serving as Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata, from 1803 to 1804.

Henry R. Hoisington (1801–1858) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Williams College and Auburn Theological Seminary. He served as a missionary with the American Ceylon Mission and as instructor and principal at Batticotta Seminary until 1849.

Henry Rawlinson (1810–1895) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He served the Royal Asiatic Society as Director in 1862 and as President from 1878 to 1881.
Henry Rice (b. 1846) was an Indologist who served as a missionary for the London Missionary Society (~1869–1880) and subsequently for the Church of Scotland (1880–1905).

Henry Snyder Gehman (1888–1981) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, earning a Ph.D. at Penn. He taught Semitic languages at Princeton University (1929–1935) and served as Professor of Old Testament at Princeton Theological Seminary (1930–1958).
Henry Steel Olcott (1832–1907) was an active figure in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia University (~1847–1849) and founded the Theosophical Society in 1875.

Henry Sullivan Jarrett (1839–1919) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Prior Park College. He served in the Government of India's Legislative Department (~1870–1877) and as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners, Fort William (1870–1894).
